title: Learning Patterns-Guided Data Generation for Knowledge Tracing

problem.claim: Knowledge tracing monitors and forecasts students' knowledge states to support personalized education.

gap.claim: Existing knowledge tracing approaches primarily focus on model-centric sequence modeling and do not exploit information from data sparsity, limiting performance.

contributions.claim: LPDG is a data-centric knowledge tracing paradigm that generates student-exercise interaction data by revealing learning patterns and generating ideal training data.
A learning-patterns-guided exercise sequence regenerator combines a Transformer with a pattern enhancer to extract information for generating training data.
A learning-patterns-guided pseudo-label generator uses a diffusion process to construct pseudo-labels for regenerated sequences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across datasets are reported to demonstrate the efficacy of LPDG.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge tracing supports monitoring and forecasting students' knowledge states for personalized education.
Model-centric approaches overlook information in data sparsity, limiting performance.
LPDG addresses the gap through learning-pattern-guided generation of ideal training data.
The framework regenerates exercise sequences, generates diffusion-based pseudo-labels, incorporates generated data into training, and integrates with model-centric KT approaches.
The authors report efficacy across datasets.

source_observation.claim: The paper identifies unused information in data sparsity as a limitation of existing model-centric approaches.

interpretation.claim: Improving a sequence-modeling task may involve augmenting or restructuring the data rather than only changing the predictive model.

application.claim: For sparse interaction data, consider pattern-guided regeneration and pseudo-labeling before or alongside model changes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when generated data improves knowledge tracing or how the approach behaves under different sparsity conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the learning patterns or the pattern enhancer in detail.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or generalization conditions.
